reasons.D: Sun-halo priestess: a rayed gold sun disc behind the head, the clearest sun-worship read from every camera, over a pale V-neck bodice, terracotta belt and pleated stone skirt (second critic 6.25, first; first critic 6.45, second).
reasons.F: Terracotta bell: the run's best skirt, a clean A-line flaring from a belted waist that holds on the slim avatar, under a stepped ziggurat crown; its sleeves are the slimmest in the run (the blue at the shoulders is the preview dummy's bare upper arm) (5.85, second; first critic 6.68, first).
reasons.B: Temple gown: the most Grashan outline, a stepped ziggurat headdress over stepped temple tiers in pale stone with terracotta and gold lips, a gown carved from the ruins (5.4, third).

fixes.D: The pleated skirt hangs straight: splay it into a flare with a stepped stone hem, and halve the sleeve blocks.
fixes.F: Put a slim pale under-sleeve on the upper arm so the avatar doesn't show, lighten the terracotta and add a pale hem band; the back is plain dark grey.
fixes.B: The stacked slab sleeves are wider than the shoulders and the top reads as a walking building: narrow sleeves, a tapered bodice, fewer and taller skirt tiers.

notes: 6 of 6 survived the draft and the rework with no resume (g01 and g04 hit the 40-turn rework cap with their sets still passing). The slim-sleeve ask in the brief mostly did not land: both critics found shoulder-wide block sleeves on five of six; only F narrowed them, and then the bare dummy arm showed. All six backs are plain dark grey. The best gown would be D's halo and bodice over F's A-line with B's stepped hem.
